title: Al-Ba'ith, the Resurrector
hookLine: the Resurrector, who raises the dead
tomorrow: interview day. who sees the part nobody's watching?

cards: A Houston summer: the yard cracked, the grass the color of straw. Then a storm rolls through, and that smell rises off the hot pavement, sharp and green.
Dadi's tomato plants on the back step looked finished last week; her knee has kept her from tending them. This morning there are new leaves. She sends Amira a photo with one word: see?
Amira zooms in on the green. So what does rain on dry ground have to do with the end of everything?

teach.b: The Qur'an points at that exact thing and makes a claim about it.

Surah Fatir: "And Allah it is Who sendeth the winds and they raise a cloud; then We lead it unto a dead land and revive therewith the earth after its death. Such is the Resurrection." Rain on dry ground is the preview.

That's today's Name: Al-Ba'ith, the Resurrector, the one who raises. In Surah Al-Hajj it's said plainly: Allah will raise those who are in the graves. The Qur'an doesn't ask you to picture the raising out of nothing.
It hands you a smell, a sprout, a field going green, and says: like that. Here's the detail to tell a friend tonight.
The Prophet Muhammad, peace be upon him, taught a line for waking up, in Sahih al-Bukhari: praise be to Allah, who gave us life after He had caused us to die, and to Him is the rising.
The Qur'an itself speaks of sleep as a kind of taking of the soul.
So every morning is a small raising. You've been through it every day of your life, and called it waking up. That makes Al-Ba'ith a Name for small things too.
A habit dropped during a hard month isn't buried for good: a morning prayer, a page of Qur'an, the sketchbook, the run.
The one who raises a field can raise those. Not by willpower alone. Like rain.

how: Muslims say on waking, from a hadith in Sahih al-Bukhari, praise to Allah who gave life after death and to whom is the rising; belief in the resurrection is part of the Muslim creed.

o: the Resurrector, who raises the dead
the one who sends storms on the proud
the one who keeps the dead at rest

games.q: signs of the rising — tap the pairs.
p: a dead land revived by rain

s: the Qur'an asks people to imagine the resurrection out of nothing
it points to rain reviving dead earth: "Such is the Resurrection" (35:9).
a waking-up line in Sahih al-Bukhari thanks Allah for life after a kind of death
praise to Allah, who gave us life after He caused us to die, and to Him is the rising.
once a good habit is dropped for long, it's gone for good
the lesson's point: the one who raises a dead field can raise a habit too.

games.q: a friend who quit piano a year ago says, 'it's dead. i'm too far behind now.' what fits today's Name?
o: 'dry ground comes back with rain. play one song this week.'
'it's gone; better to find something new to start.'
'wait until you feel inspired, then go all in.'
games.why: 35:9 pictures dead land revived by rain. a small first watering is how the green starts.

practice: Find one object tied to a good habit you've let go: a prayer mat, running shoes, a sketchbook, a Qur'an on a high shelf. Hold it in your hands and feel its weight, its texture, maybe its dust.
Notice whether it's heavier or lighter than you expected. Then set it where you'll see it first thing tomorrow morning, and sit.

wordCard.voice: Al-Ba'ith. The Resurrector, who raises the dead, and the dry field, and the morning. Name forty-nine.

orig.note: Arabic: the Resurrector, the one who raises. 22:7: Allah will raise those who are in the graves.

carryVoice: Carry this: he raises, and dry ground isn't the end of the story. Almost fifty now.

sources.q: And Allah it is Who sendeth the winds and they raise a cloud; then We lead it unto a dead land and revive therewith the earth after its death. Such is the Resurrection.

sources.ref: Qur'an 22:7 (Allah will raise those who are in the graves)
Qur'an 39:42 (Allah takes the souls at death, and those that die not, in their sleep)
Sahih al-Bukhari 6312 (the waking du'a: praise to Allah who gave us life after causing us to die, and to Him is the rising)
